# Patient registration (his-backend `patient` + `encounter` GraphQL, his-backend REST, his-frontend registration form)

**Goal:** a registration officer can register a patient once, get a unique medical record number, and find the
patient again — without the form silently dropping data, without an unauthenticated caller writing PHI, and
without the frontend reporting a failure as a success.

**Docs:** test doc [patient-registration-testing.md](../../patient-registration-testing.md) · module features: [module catalogue](../../modules/README.md) (linked on every story).

Epic code `PATREG`. Source of the stories and findings:
`his-v3-ai/services-impl/202611/backend-rest-e2e-qa-assessment/data-integration/D-HISV3-PATIENT-REGISTRATION/`
(`USER-STORIES.md` → `US-D-HISV3-PATIENT-REGISTRATION-01..17`, `USER-SCENARIOS.md` →
`SC-D-HISV3-PATIENT-REGISTRATION-01..08`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` §6 → findings `PR-01..PR-38`).

The story ids of this catalog are short (`US-PATREG-NN`); the mapping is one to one:
`US-PATREG-01` = `US-D-HISV3-PATIENT-REGISTRATION-01`, and so on.

## User stories

- **US-PATREG-01** ([A01.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-01), [A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05)) — As a registration officer I want to register a new patient with the complete data so that the patient gets a master identity and a permanent medical record number.
- **US-PATREG-02** ([A01.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-01), [A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05)) — As a registration officer I want the system to tell me when an identity is already registered so that no two master records are created for one person.
- **US-PATREG-03** ([A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05)) — As a registration officer I want the medical record number to be unique and sequential so that no two patients share one.
- **US-PATREG-04** ([A01.07](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-07), [A02.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a02-01)) — As a counter officer I want a registration number at check-in so that the queue is unambiguous.
- **US-PATREG-05** ([A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05), [A14.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a14-01)) — As a registration officer I want a national patient to be registered in SATUSEHAT so that the record is interoperable.
- **US-PATREG-06** ([A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05), [A01.06](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-06)) — As a registration officer I want the phone number verified over WhatsApp so that the hospital can reach the patient.
- **US-PATREG-07** ([A01.03](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-03)) — As an ER officer I want to register an emergency patient quickly so that treatment can start before the MRN exists.
- **US-PATREG-08** ([A01.04](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-04), [A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05)) — As a midwife I want to register a newborn with the birth encounter so that the baby record is linked to the delivery.
- **US-PATREG-09** ([A01.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-01)) — As a medical records officer I want to correct a patient and activate a draft so that the master data stays usable.
- **US-PATREG-10** ([A01.02](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-02)) — As a medical records officer I want to merge two patient records so that the clinical history is not split.
- **US-PATREG-11** ([A01.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-01)) — As a counter officer I want to find a patient I just registered so that I can continue to check-in.
- **US-PATREG-12** ([A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05)) — As an integrator I want the creation to be atomic and retry-safe so that there is no half-created or duplicated patient.
- **US-PATREG-13** ([A01.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-01), [A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05)) — As a security officer I want every surface that writes or reads patient data to require authentication so that PHI is not exposed.
- **US-PATREG-14** ([A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05)) — As a registration officer I want everything I typed to be stored so that I do not have to type it twice.
- **US-PATREG-15** ([A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05)) — As an officer I want an actionable failure message so that I know what to correct.
- **US-PATREG-16** ([A01.05](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-05)) — As an integrator I want consistent numbering and data quality so that reports and third-party integrations are accurate.
- **US-PATREG-17** ([A01.01](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-01), [A01.02](../../modules/A-core.md#f-a01-02)) — As an auditor I want to know who registered, changed, activated and merged a patient so that every master-data change is traceable.

## Defect ids

The findings of the cluster documentation keep their `PR-nn` number and get a defect id of this suite:
`DEF-801` = PR-01, `DEF-802` = PR-02, `DEF-803` = PR-03, … `DEF-838` = PR-38 (the number is `800` + the
finding number). The rows that pin a finding are marked `xfail` in the scenario text; they are automated as
**expected failures** (`test.fail()` + a `defect` annotation), so a fix shows up as an "unexpectedly passed".

Four findings were **not** in the cluster documentation — they came out of the first live run against staging
(2026-11-09) and got the next free ids:

| Defect    | Finding                                                                                                                | Evidence                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEF-840` | the registration never returns the medical record number — `noRM` is an empty string                                   | `CreatePatientFull` drops the MRN (`his-backend/internal/service/patient/patient.go:1258`); the resolver maps the _input_ DTO, which has no `NoRM` (`pkg/dto/patient/patient_full_input_dto.go:223`) |
| `DEF-841` | an identifier that is already registered is not refused — the second registration returns the patient of the first one | the guard asks `IsPractitionerExisted(personID)`, which answers _true_ for every person (`internal/storage/practitioner/practitioner.go:834`)                                                        |
| `DEF-842` | `patientCheckEmailIsExist` rejects every valid e-mail ("tidak valid") and lets every malformed one through             | the condition is inverted (`pkg/graph/patient/resolvers/patientfull.resolvers.go:1565`): `if common.IsValidEmail(email)`                                                                             |
| `DEF-843` | `telecom.statusCode` and `email.statusCode` are never written, although the contract exposes them                      | `person_telecom.status_code` / `person_email.status_code` stay empty after a registration                                                                                                            |

## Status of this catalog

Written 2026-11-09 from the static reading of `his-backend@staging` (3743680c2),
`his-frontend@feat/alert-unset-SIP-practitioner-091126` (ad5aeb9c2) and `his-go-modules@staging` (f13c3c59a).

**The specs were executed against staging on 2026-11-09** (GraphQL `patient` + `encounter`, REST
`/api/v1/patients` + `/api/v1/encounters`, and the form of `his-frontend`), with an impersonated session
(`Sup3rAdm1n`). A row is `automated` when its spec exists **and passes**; a row that pins an open defect is
`blocked` with the reason `defect:DEF-nnn` — the spec runs as an expected failure, so a fix shows up as an
"unexpectedly passed". Rows that need the staging DB credential (`~/.config/staging-his-v3-db/…json`, not
available on the author workstation) or another prerequisite stay `blocked` with that reason.

Two findings of the cluster documentation did not reproduce on the deployed build and therefore carry no
expected failure: **PR-32** (the identifier is not written to the browser console — `TC-PATREG-062` asserts
the behaviour) and **PR-17**'s REST counterpart is covered by `TC-PATREG-055`/`056`.
